import html # A minimal HTML template with a placeholder for user content. html_template = """ Safe Output
{user_content}
""" def render_html_output(user_input: str) -> str: """ Return an HTML page that safely embeds the provided user input. The function escapes any characters that could otherwise form executable HTML/JavaScript, mitigating XSS and CWE-707 concerns. If the placeholder is missing from the template an exception will be raised, making the bug obvious during development. Parameters: user_input (str): Raw text provided by a user. Returns: str: A fully formed HTML document with the escaped user content. """ # Escape special characters to prevent script injection safe_content = html.escape(user_input, quote=True) # Ensure the placeholder exists in the template if "{user_content}" not in html_template: raise ValueError("The HTML template does not contain a {user_content} placeholder.") # Insert the escaped content into the template return html_template.format(user_content=safe_content)
